Arab News reports that US Vance is considering direct diplomacy with Iran to end the war, and BBC Persian reports on his efforts to negotiate with Mohsen Rezaei. Trump says the war seems to be nearing its end. Iran has denied negotiating with the US, so no talks are confirmed.

Iran threatens US military bases in Europe, conditional on their being used to attack Iranian territory, according to reports in several countries. Iran also denies negotiating with the US and says it continues to blockade Hormuz (Iranian statements as reported by Taiwanese outlet newtalk.tw).

Iran says it will not let enriched nuclear material leave the country, according to its security chief. Iran's military also reportedly updated its target list with no geographical limits on retaliatory strikes (Middle East Eye, single source).

Iran's threats widened: outlets in several countries report that Tehran threatens US bases from the Middle East to Europe, and an Iranian official reportedly threatened Trump and Netanyahu. A senior official says these bases would be targeted if the US renews attacks.

cyber.title: Iran-linked intrusions into US water controllers
cyber.method: Intrusions into industrial controllers from Rockwell, Schneider Electric and Siemens.
cyber.summary: ABC reported in August that water-sector intrusions reached at least 12 states, with no widespread supply disruption. The IRGC-linked group CyberAv3ngers claimed the campaign, per CSIS. NBC reported unsuccessful attempts on US telecom and energy systems.
cyber.us_why: The intrusions happened in the US. The FBI, NSA, DOE and CISA warned that Iranian actors target these controllers, but the US government has not publicly attributed the campaign.
cyber.what_to_watch: Any new CISA advisory, or a water-supply disruption tied to these controllers.

sources.text: NBC News reported on Sept 2, citing four sources, that Iranian hackers also tried to reach US telecom and energy systems. The attempts were reported as unsuccessful so far.
CSIS's incident list says the IRGC-linked CyberAv3ngers claimed the August water campaign across at least a dozen states. It says the US government had not publicly attributed it.

ABC News reported on Aug 4, citing sources, that water-sector intrusions reached at least 12 states, with Iran the prime suspect. Involvement was unconfirmed and supplies saw no widespread disruption.

TechCrunch reports an updated advisory from the FBI, NSA, DOE and CISA. It says Iranian actors target controllers from Rockwell, Schneider Electric and Siemens. Those products are also used in the US.

actions.summary: Taken together, the actions point to long-horizon readiness rather than preparation for a specific date. In Europe and Russia that means reservists, cable protection and home kits. In the Middle East, steps continue even as the US talks of a near deal with Iran and talks run in Abu Dhabi. This window added little that is sudden: Britain's undersea-protection funding, another Russian region's reserve recruitment, and the Polisario Front's mobilisation call.

patterns.title: Reserve, mobilisation and undersea-protection steps around Russia and NATO's east
patterns.points_to: On both sides, these steps build the ability to grow forces quickly and to guard cables and seabed infrastructure over years. The threat they name is hybrid attack and a possible wider war, not a set date. Britain's £90 million for submarine-hunting drones and AI adds a seabed layer to the reservist training in Poland, Norway, Finland and France.
patterns.unsaid: Russia kept building reserves in Bashkortostan and Chelyabinsk while US-mediated talks ran in Abu Dhabi on 10–11 November. The timing suggests Moscow is keeping its options open whatever the talks produce. The European steps are consistent with planning for the period after any ceasefire, which the Dutch defence ministry flagged in June as a risk window.
patterns.plain_explanation: Most of this belongs to long-running programmes: Russia's BARS reserve, its regular autumn conscription round, NATO force targets and larger defence budgets. Germany's defence minister also says conscription is likely unnecessary for now.
